name: MiniCPM-V 4.7 (35B-A3B and 1B)

lineage.base_model: Qwen3.5-architecture language models (config model_type qwen3_5_moe_text for 35B-A3B, qwen3_5_text for 1B); the card does not name the initialization checkpoint
lineage.how_derived: vision-language model with a 27-layer ViT using intra-ViT early token compression (LLaVA-UHD v4); first MoE model of the MiniCPM-V series

purpose: Single-image, multi-image and video understanding for on-device and local use; the 35B-A3B variant targets smooth on-device MoE inference (phones, tablets) without capability loss, the 1B variant the smallest footprint.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card tag apache-2.0 on all repos; LICENSE text not opened.

architecture.kind: hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention MoE with ViT vision encoder (35B-A3B); dense 1B
architecture.gguf_arch: qwen35moe (language model of the 35B-A3B, inferred from config model_type qwen3_5_moe_text; mmproj separate)
architecture.drafter: DSpark drafter heads (35B-A3B-DSpark 0.78 GB, 1B-DSpark), BF16 and GGUF; the 1B config also lists an MTP layer
architecture.why_this_design: Card: early compression inside the ViT reduces compute of later encoder layers and supports mixed 4x/16x visual token compression; the MoE is made on-device-capable by Lookahead Expert Scheduling (cross-layer routing prediction preloads the next layer's experts, computation still follows the real router), fine-grained layer-wise quantization of expert weights and DSpark speculative sampling. The 1B layer count (24) is from config.json.

variants.notes: IQ3_XS 14.48, IQ3_M 15.44, IQ4_XS 18.73, Q4_0 19.71, IQ4_NL 19.78, Q4_1 21.85, F16 69.38; language model only, mmproj files separate (a 4x mmproj exists); thinking/ subfolder with a thinking template

pc-12gb.notes: a user reports 37.5 tok/s with vision on an 8 GB RTX 2060 Super with 32 GB RAM using cpu-moe, q4_0 KV cache and the DSpark drafter (llama.cpp, HF discussion 13); IQ3_M 15.4 GB nearly fits VRAM

pc-16gb.notes: 21.2 GB file against 13.6 GB VRAM budget, rest from RAM

pc-24gb.notes: a user ran Q4_K_M on 24 GB VRAM with 64 GB RAM (discussion 10)

mac-16-24gb.notes: 14.5 GB against a 12 GB GPU share; the vendor demos a 3 GB on-device mode (SSD streaming with LES) on a phone, not a general Mac recipe

mac-32gb.notes: 21.2 GB against about 22 GB GPU share, tight with vision and KV

engine_support.notes: Official GGUF with llama.cpp and DSpark speculative decoding works per user report; LES lives in OpenBMB's llama.cpp-omni fork. Tona has a qwen35moe path for the language side, the vision tower and DSpark are not implemented.

benchmarks.name: Overall score vs inference time in Instruct mode
benchmarks.score: higher overall score in less time than Qwen3.6-35B-A3B

benchmarks.name: On-device decode speed, iPhone 17 Pro Max
Decode speed RTX 2060 Super 8 GB + 32 GB RAM
benchmarks.variant: Q4_K_M, cpu-moe, q4_0 KV, DSpark, vision enabled

benchmarks.name: NanoBench 12 coding/agentic/system tasks (OMP harness, reasoning off)

strengths: MoE with vision at 3 B active runs on an 8 GB GPU with RAM offload (user report)
Official quantized GGUF and DSpark drafter at release
Early-compressed visual tokens (4x/16x) make images cheap
weaknesses: Benchmark numbers on the card are images only, not text
A discussion questions the vendor's reproduction of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B numbers (MMMU-Pro 69.9 against 75.3 official); vendor reply pending in the text read
Needs transformers >= 5.18 for the BF16 path
soft.behavior: Instruct and thinking templates are shipped as separate GGUF template sets (thinking/ folder).
best_for: image and video understanding on 12 to 32 GB machines

user_reports.summary: 37.5 tok/s with vision on an RTX 2060 Super 8 GB, Ryzen 5 5600G, 32 GB RAM; draft n_max tuning matters because RAM latency bounds the model
NanoBench local run (24 GB VRAM, 64 GB RAM): 9/12 tasks in two harnesses, called very fast

soft.maturity: OpenBMB ships MiniCPM-V since 2024; 869k downloads of the 35B-A3B repo and 423k of its GGUF within six weeks; 20 discussion threads.

tona_fit.reason: A vision-capable A3B MoE with an official GGUF and the architecture family Tona already runs on the text side (Qwen3.5 MoE), plus LES, a prior-art technique for expert prefetch (relevant to our expert streaming). The vision tower would have to be added; text quality relative to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is unverified.
blockers: vision tower and mmproj not implemented in Tona
numbers only as images, no independent coding result

sources.note: discussion text via the HF API

open_questions: Numeric vision and text benchmark tables (images on the card)
Initialization checkpoint of the language model (Qwen3.5 architecture, base not stated)
